# libfobos

**Host library and command-line tools for the RigExpert Fobos SDR receiver**

- **Version recorded:** 2.4.1
- **Categories:** `sdr-hardware`
- **Upstream:** <https://github.com/rigexpert/libfobos>

## What it does

The host side of the RigExpert Fobos SDR, a USB software defined radio receiver: a shared library (libfobos) that opens the board, tunes it and streams samples, and three command-line programs. `fobos_devinfo` lists the boards and prints their hardware revision, firmware version and serial, `fobos_recorder` records samples to a WAV file, and `fobos_fwloader` writes firmware to the board. The library's API is receive-only: it sets a frequency, gain and sample rate and reads samples, and has no transmit call.

## Why you would want it

It is the layer the SoapySDR module (`soapysdr-module-fobos`), and through it SDR++, GQRX and GNU Radio, reach the board through, and `fobos_devinfo` is the first check that the board and its permissions are right before an application is involved. RigExpert sells the Fobos as an HF-to-microwave wideband receiver; this project has not measured its coverage or sensitivity (D-027) and quotes none.

## Before it will work

A Fobos SDR, which the maintainer does not own, and the udev rule and `plugdev` membership from the `fobos-sdr` hardware entry (`hammunition hardware apply`). Upstream's versions.txt, at v.2.3.2, says "please update the firmware to v.2.1.1" and "HW rev 3.0.0 or higher only"; `fobos_fwloader` writes firmware. The sibling library `libfobos-sdr-agile` says it supports revision 4 natively and revisions 2 and 3 only with special firmware.

## Install and launch

- **Installed by name only** — it is in no profile.
- **Install:** `hammunition install libfobos --dry-run`, read the plan, then run it without `--dry-run`.
- **Launch:** Commands it leaves on your PATH: `fobos_devinfo`, `fobos_recorder`, `fobos_fwloader`.
- **The install needs the network to:** the upstream files the plan lists, each checked against a pinned digest (or, for map and reference data, the publisher or a LAN mirror).

## Known problems

**The board presents the same USB identifier (16d0:132e) under two firmware families**, the original and the "agile" one, and tells them apart only by the device descriptor's bcdDevice: this library opens bcdDevice 0x0000 and its sibling libfobos-sdr-agile opens 0x0101. Loading the wrong firmware makes the board invisible to the library you have, not broken. Builds install into /usr/local and the library is found through an embedded run path, so a program of your own that links it needs `-L/usr/local/lib -Wl,-rpath,/usr/local/lib` or `ldconfig`. This is an untagged pin: the unit is built from a commit, not a release. **Not measured:** everything that needs a board, including firmware writes.
